subject: Data boundary cleanup timeline — DPA retention & deletion Q&A
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>, Mark Johnson <m.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on data boundary cleanup & retention timing for DPA

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking a look at our DPA draft earlier today. A couple of points the legal and engineering teams asked me to clarify so we can get a clean redline back to procurement:

1) Deletion timing: The draft currently says "Customer data will be deleted within 30 days of termination." Could you confirm whether that 30-day window applies to: (a) primary live data only, or (b) live data + backups + KV/prefix caches? Our compliance folks are pushing for an explicit timeline for backups and ephemeral caches.

2) Proof of deletion: We need a short description of the evidence Redwood can provide after deletion — is a certificate/attestation available? If so, what is the expected turnaround?

3) Geofence cleanup: Our policy requires that, for EU-subject data that was served from US-region hardware during failover, there is a clear playbook for moving or deleting those copies. Does Redwood offer a documented "boundary cleanup" timeline when data crosses regions temporarily?

4) On-demand erasure requests from data subjects: SLA expectations (how soon can you remove all traces including cached tokens / KV caches / snapshots that might include the data?)

Happy to hop on a short call, but if you can point us to the specific DPA language you propose for these four items that will speed review. We need to finalise by end of month.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health

---
Note: attaching a consolidated list of our in-scope datasets in a follow-up email.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on data boundary cleanup & retention timing for DPA

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Quick replies inline and then Ben will add a suggested redline you can review.

1) Deletion timing: The 30-day language in our standard DPA covers persistent production data and any snapshot backups that are retained for operational restore. Ephemeral caches (KV/prefix caches, in-memory accelerators) are treated separately — these are typically evicted much faster (minutes/hours) and not part of the 30-day backup window.

2) Proof of deletion: We can provide a deletion certificate that references the deletion event ids, storage locations, and time ranges. Typical turnaround: 5 business days after the deletion job completes. For backups that require longer retention due to legal hold, we can provide status and an expected deletion schedule.

3) Geofence cleanup: We have an internal "boundary cleanup" playbook: temporary cross-region copies created for failover are flagged for prioritized cleanup during the first scheduled wipe window (default 7–14 days), and a full onshore purge of backup copies is targeted within the 30-day erase window. I will ask Ben to propose explicit DPA wording.

4) On-demand erasure: For subject access / erasure requests we aim to remove entries from live indices and caches within 48 hours and complete snapshot/backups sweep within 30 days, subject to lawful hold exceptions. We do not guarantee deletion from third-party analytics vendors that have separately ingested data unless covered by the DPA.

I'll loop in Ben with a redline; if Acme wants tighter SLAs for backups (e.g., 7-day backup wipe) that's something we can evaluate under a Dedicated/Private deployment or as an addendum.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed DPA redline: explicit timing and proof language

Hi Samantha — attaching a short redline ("DPA_redline_proposal_20260115.docx") that tries to capture the commitments Jordan outlined and provides explicit language you can drop into your contract. Key points included: 

- "Deletion window": Persistent production data and backups: full deletion within 30 calendar days of contract termination or data deletion request, except where legal hold applies.
- "Ephemeral caches": Any in-memory or prefix/KV caches containing customer data will be evicted as part of normal cache lifecycle (typically minutes to 24 hours); Redwood will target cache purge within 48 hours for on-demand erasure requests.
- "Cross-region copies": If temporary cross-region copies are created during failover, Redwood will mark such copies for prioritized deletion and will remove them from hot storage within 14 days and from backup archives within the 30-day deletion window.
- "Proof of deletion": Redwood will provide a signed deletion attestation listing the deletion job id, affected object prefixes, and timestamps within 5 business days of request completion.

Notes / caveats in the redline: for customers with Dedicated or Private deployments we can discuss narrower backup wipe SLAs and additional on-prem sweep tooling. Also, backup rotations and immutable offsite archives (if specifically requested) may have different handling — we call that out as an exception.

Attach: DPA_redline_proposal_20260115.docx (redline with three options: standard (30 days), accelerated backup wipe (14 days, addl fee), private-dedicated (7 days))

If any of this is too permissive, let us know which exact clause you'd like tightened and Ben (me) will push to Engineering/Infra for technical feasibility and any cost impact.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Solutions – Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_redline_proposal_20260115.docx (redline with three options: standard (30 days), accelerated backup wipe (14 days, addl fee), private-dedicated (7 days))

Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redline: explicit timing and proof language

Hi Samantha — a couple of compliance clarifications from Legal that I asked Ben to include in the second pass of redlines: 

- Backup carveouts: We will explicitly exclude immutable third-party cold storage (if used) from the standard 30-day purge; if Acme requires deletion from those archives we need to identify them and may require a separate agreement for retrieval+purge.

- Proof-of-erasure template: I've added a short template (proof_of_erasure_template.docx) that enumerates job IDs, object key prefixes, UTC timestamps, and the operator signature. The template also includes a checkbox for "legal hold applied" when applicable.

- Escrow / e-discovery hold: If Acme issues a legal hold, Redwood will suspend scheduled deletion and notify Acme with a list of affected datasets and expected hold duration. We can support onshore access for e-discovery if requested and scoped.

Ben — when you upload the next redline, can you also include a line referencing our SOC 2 attestation as supplemental evidence and a stub for the deletion certificate? I've attached SOC2_Attestation_stub.pdf to this thread for initial review.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Jordan/Ben/Neha — thanks for the quick follow-up and for the proposed redlines. A few items from Acme Legal before we move to procurement: 

1) We appreciate the separation of ephemeral caches vs backups. For assurances to our internal risk committee we would like the redline to include a hard statement that cache eviction for on-demand erasure will be "targeted within 48 hours and confirmed via attestation." Please include that exact phrasing in the final clause.

2) For cross-region copies: Acme will accept the 14-day hot-storage + 30-day backup purge as long as Redwood includes a table in the DPA appendix that lists the default wipe windows and the escalation path if a copy is discovered after the window.

3) Proof of deletion: Accept 5 business days for the attestation. Please confirm the attestation will include the operator signature (digital) and the UTC timestamps.

4) SOC 2: Can you provide the latest SOC 2 report to Acme's security mailbox (security@acmehealth.com)? The stub is fine for now but the team needs the full report under NDA.

If you can submit a final redline with the two attachments (redline .docx + proof_of_erasure template) and a link to the SOC2 under NDA by EOD Friday, Acme Procurement believes we can close this DPA next week. Also can we get a DocuSign link once both parties agree?

Thanks — appreciate the pragmatic tradeoffs here.

Samantha Reed
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Acme Health
